answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying each identity to a scarce stake that grows only through sustained useful work. Like an orchard that yields fruit only after seasons of tending, reputation should accrue slowly from completed tasks witnessed by independent peers. A new identity starts on a narrow ledge with small transaction limits, and only a long, checkable history earns passage to the broad mesa of full trust. Creating thousands of fake identities then buys nothing, because none has the proven record the system rewards.
